faq.q: What is the best time of day for dolphin watching in Marbella?
faq.a: The best time is early morning (8–10am) when seas are calm and dolphins are often feeding. Late afternoon (5–7pm) is a close second, with the added bonus of a sunset backdrop. Midday trips are possible but sightings can be less predictable.

faq.q: Are dolphins more active in the morning or at sunset?
faq.a: Both are good. Mornings typically have calmer water and less boat traffic, making it easier to spot dolphins. Sunsets offer warmer light and a more atmospheric experience. We recommend morning for the highest sighting probability.

faq.q: Which months are best for dolphin watching in Marbella?
faq.a: May through October is prime season. June and September tend to have the most consistent sightings, with water temperatures around 20–24°C. Dolphins are present year-round, but winter seas can be rougher, reducing sighting chances.

faq.q: What types of dolphins can I see in Marbella?
faq.a: The most common are bottlenose dolphins and striped dolphins. Occasionally, you might spot common dolphins or even pilot whales further offshore. Sightings are not guaranteed, but our skippers know the best areas.

faq.q: How long is a typical dolphin watching trip from Puerto Banús?
faq.a: Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39) offer 2-hour and 8-hour charters. A 2-hour trip is ideal for a quick dolphin encounter; the 8-hour option lets you explore further along the coast and increases your chances of multiple sightings.

faq.q: What should I bring on a dolphin watching trip?
faq.a: Sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses are essential. A light jacket is useful for early mornings or evenings. Bring a camera with a zoom lens – dolphins often approach the boat. All drinks and snacks are provided on board.

faq.q: Can I book a private dolphin watching charter?
faq.a: Yes, all our charters are private. You can choose from the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) for smaller groups, or the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) for a larger party. Contact us via WhatsApp for availability.

data.body_html:
If you're planning a dolphin watching trip in Marbella, the time of day you choose can make all the difference. Dolphins are not on a fixed schedule, but their behaviour follows predictable patterns tied to feeding, light, and sea conditions. In this guide, we break down the marbella dolphin watching best time of day, so you can maximise your chances of a memorable encounter.

Why Morning Trips Offer the Best Sighting Odds

Early morning, between 8:00 and 10:00, is widely considered the prime window. The sea is usually calm after the overnight lull, with fewer boats on the water. Dolphins are often actively hunting for breakfast, making them more visible at the surface. Our skippers at Puerto Banús recommend a morning departure for the highest probability of spotting pods.

The Sunset Alternative: Atmosphere Over Certainty

Late afternoon, from 17:00 to 19:00, offers a different kind of magic. While dolphin activity can be slightly less predictable, the golden light over the Sierra Blanca and La Concha makes for stunning photography. A sunset charter on the Astondoa 40 or Azimut 39 combines dolphin watching with a coastal cruise past the Golden Mile – a popular choice for couples.

Seasonal Patterns: When to Go for Peak Sightings

Dolphins are present off Marbella year-round, but the best months are May to October. June and September typically offer the most consistent sightings, with water temperatures between 20°C and 24°C. In summer, early morning trips are cooler and more comfortable, while autumn afternoons can be equally productive.

Our Fleet and Departure Times

All our boats depart from Puerto Banús. For a 2-hour dolphin-focused trip, the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) are ideal – both are priced at €749 for 2 hours, including skipper, drinks, and snacks. For a full-day adventure, the 8-hour charter at €2,299 lets you explore further towards Cabopino or Estepona. Larger groups can opt for the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) at €4,719 for 4 hours, which includes a free jet ski.

What to Expect on Board

Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, and safety equipment – all with Spanish IVA included. No hidden costs. Our skippers know the local waters intimately and will adjust the route based on real-time sightings.

Practical Tips for a Successful Trip

  • Book an early morning slot (8:00–10:00) for the best chance of sightings.
  • Bring sunscreen and a hat – even in the morning, the sun is strong.
  • Use a zoom lens; dolphins often approach the boat but can stay at a distance.
  • Dress in layers – sea breezes can be cool, especially in spring or autumn.
  • Check the weather forecast – calm seas (Beaufort 0–2) are ideal.

Combine Dolphin Watching with a Coastal Cruise

A dolphin watching trip doesn't have to be a single-purpose outing. You can combine it with a visit to Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés for a swim, or cruise towards Sotogrande for lunch. The 8-hour charter gives you plenty of time to do both. For more ideas, see our [main boat rental guide](/).

Booking Your Dolphin Watching Charter

Ready to go? Contact us via WhatsApp for availability and pricing on any of our boats. For smaller groups, the Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Speedboat (7m, 6 pax) are budget-friendly options, though we recommend the Tier A boats for the best balance of comfort and speed. Remember, the early bird catches the dolphin – book your morning slot today.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best time of day for dolphin watching in Marbella?

The best time is early morning (8–10am) when seas are calm and dolphins are often feeding. Late afternoon (5–7pm) is a close second, with the added bonus of a sunset backdrop. Midday trips are possible but sightings can be less predictable.

Are dolphins more active in the morning or at sunset?

Both are good. Mornings typically have calmer water and less boat traffic, making it easier to spot dolphins. Sunsets offer warmer light and a more atmospheric experience. We recommend morning for the highest sighting probability.

Which months are best for dolphin watching in Marbella?

May through October is prime season. June and September tend to have the most consistent sightings, with water temperatures around 20–24°C. Dolphins are present year-round, but winter seas can be rougher, reducing sighting chances.

What types of dolphins can I see in Marbella?

The most common are bottlenose dolphins and striped dolphins. Occasionally, you might spot common dolphins or even pilot whales further offshore. Sightings are not guaranteed, but our skippers know the best areas.

How long is a typical dolphin watching trip from Puerto Banús?

Our Tier A boats (Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39) offer 2-hour and 8-hour charters. A 2-hour trip is ideal for a quick dolphin encounter; the 8-hour option lets you explore further along the coast and increases your chances of multiple sightings.

What should I bring on a dolphin watching trip?

Sunscreen, a hat, and sunglasses are essential. A light jacket is useful for early mornings or evenings. Bring a camera with a zoom lens – dolphins often approach the boat. All drinks and snacks are provided on board.

Can I book a private dolphin watching charter?

Yes, all our charters are private. You can choose from the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5m, 11 pax) for smaller groups, or the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) for a larger party. Contact us via WhatsApp for availability.
